changes: original_meaning 收为两条借入线共同的拉丁语源头 novellus 的 gloss「新的，幼小的」，并在 how 链中分开形容词线与名词线（现行路径把小说义从形容词『新的』直跳，缺意大利语 novella 这一环）。
semantic_path 重建三站，how 补名词义的薄伽丘短篇起点（1560 年代）与长篇化年代（1630 年代）。
evidence: Etymonline: "novel (n.) \"fictitious prose narrative,\" 1560s, from Italian novella \"short story,\" originally \"new story, news,\" from Latin novella \"new things\"... Originally \"one of the tales or short stories in a collection\" (especially Boccaccio's), later (1630s) \"long prose fiction narrative or tale,\" a type of work which had before that been called a romance."
Etymonline: "novel (adj.) \"new, strange, unusual, previously unknown,\" mid-15c.... from Latin novellus \"new, young, recent,\" diminutive of novus \"new\""
novel.mechanism_sentence: novel 全家都出自拉丁语 novus「新」：形容词线是「新颖、新奇」；名词线经意大利语 novella「新鲜故事」而来——故事越讲越长，1630 年代起就成了长篇「小说」。

semantic_path.how: 经古法语 novel 进入英语（15 世纪中）：不只是『新的』，还兼『新奇的、前所未闻的』——词库的形容词义『新颖的』即此支。
名词是另一条借入线：意大利语 novella 本义『新故事、新鲜事』，原指故事集（尤其薄伽丘《十日谈》）里的一篇，1560 年代入英语指短篇故事；1630 年代故事越讲越长，转指长篇虚构叙事——这类作品此前叫 romance（Etymonline 编年）。

changes: original_meaning 大改：现行字段取的是中古法语 occurrer 的『出乎意料地发生』，属下游译义；按拉丁语 occurrere 的 gloss 改为「迎上前去，撞上」并写明构词（ob- 迎 + currere 跑）。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 明确给出的语义链（meet → present itself → appear → happen）重建，并补 1620 年代『想起』义。
evidence: Etymonline: "occur (v.) 1520s, \"meet, meet in argument,\" from French occurrer \"happen unexpectedly\" or directly from Latin occurrere \"run to meet, run against, befall, present itself,\" from ob \"against, toward\" + currere \"to run\""
Etymonline: "Sense development is from \"meet\" to \"present itself\" to \"appear\" to \"happen\" (\"present itself in the course of events\"). Meaning \"to come into one's mind\" is from 1620s."
occur.mechanism_sentence: occur 是拉丁语「迎面跑来」（ob- 迎着 + currere 跑）：事情迎面撞上你，就「发生」了；念头迎面撞进脑子，就是「想起」（occur to）。
occur.original_meaning: 迎上前去，撞上；降临到（某人）身上

semantic_path.meaning: 迎上前去，撞上；降临到（某人）身上

semantic_path.how: Etymonline 明排这条语义链：『遇上』→『自己冒出来』→『出现』→『发生』——在事件进程中迎面撞到你面前的事，就是『发生了』；英语 1520 年代入词时还带着『（论辩中）碰上』的余味。
同一个『迎面而来』用在念头上：1620 年代添 occur to 义『被想起』——想法像不速之客一样撞进脑子里。

changes: original_meaning 按拉丁语 offerre 的 gloss 改为「呈上，献给」（现行字段是把古法语与古英语两站揉在一起的含混表述）。
semantic_path 按来源重排三站并纠正顺序关系：拉丁 offerre 为源头，古英语宗教义在前、世俗义 15 世纪初经古法语回流，how 写明两段。
evidence: Etymonline: "Old English ofrian \"to bring or put forward, to make a presentation, to show, exhibit;\" also \"to sacrifice, present something solemnly or worshipfully as a religious sacrifice, bring an oblation,\" from Latin offerre \"to present, bestow, bring before\" (in Late Latin \"to present in worship\"), from... ob \"to\" + ferre \"to bring, to carry\""

Etymonline: "The Latin word was borrowed widely in Germanic languages in the religious sense via Christianity... The non-religious senses in English were from or reinforced by sense of Old French offrir \"to offer\"... From early 15c. as \"to present (something) for acceptance or rejection.\" ... Commercial sense of \"to expose for sale\" is from 1630s."
offer.mechanism_sentence: offer 是拉丁语「把东西捧到跟前」（ob- 到跟前 + ferre 拿）：古英语里它先被宗教领去当「献祭」，15 世纪起世俗义回流，才成了日常的「提供、提议」。

semantic_path.how: 拉丁词随基督教传进古英语（ofrian），宗教义占了上风：在神的面前庄重地奉上祭品（Etymonline 明言日耳曼诸语借此词多取宗教义）——广义的『呈上』先收窄成了『献祭』。
世俗义借古法语 offrir 回流：15 世纪初 offer 添『拿出来供人接受或拒绝』义，名词义『出价』1540 年代见载，动词商业义『摆出来出售』1630 年代见载——从神坛走回市集，成了今天的『提供；提议』。

changes: original_meaning 保留「橄榄油」（希腊语 elaion 的 gloss，核对无误）。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 编年重建三站：约 1300 年泛化、1520 年代石油义，how 替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "oil (n.) late 12c., \"olive oil,\" from Anglo-French and Old North French olie... from Latin oleum \"oil, olive oil\"... from Greek elaion \"olive tree,\" from elaia"

Etymonline: "In English it meant \"olive oil\" exclusively till c. 1300, when the word began to be extended to any fatty, greasy liquid substance... Use for \"petroleum\" is recorded from 1520s but not common until 19c."
oil.mechanism_sentence: oil 的源头是希腊语的「橄榄油」：约 1300 年起，它扩成一切油脂液体的总名；1520 年代又添上地底下的那一种——石油。

semantic_path.how: 地中海的特产成了北方的通名：约 1300 年起，英语 oil 不再专指橄榄油，扩到一切油滑、可燃、不溶于水的液体（词义扩大；Etymonline 编年）。
地下的『油』来认领这个名字：1520 年代已有人用 oil 指石油，19 世纪钻井业兴起后才普及——词库今义『石油』即此，油的默认主角从此换成了油田。
